children.text: Chapter 1
nirdeśe yathāvacanaṃ vigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the statement, the analysis should follow the wording exactly.

children.text: cārthe dvandvasamāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the sense of 'and', there is a <s>dvandva</s> compound.

children.text: pramāṇādīnāṃ tattvam iti śaiṣikī ṣaṣṭhī ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'the truth of the pramāṇas and so forth' uses a residual genitive.

children.text: tattvasya jñānaṃ niḥśreyasasyādhigama iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhau ||
children.translated_text: In 'knowledge of the truth is the attainment of the highest good', the genitives are objective genitives.

children.text: ta etāvanto vidyamānārthāḥ yeṣām aviparītajñānārtham ihopadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are just so many real objects, for the sake of whose non-erroneous knowledge instruction is given here.

children.text: so 'yam anavayavena tantrārtha uddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this subject matter of the system should be understood as having been stated without division into parts.

children.text: ātmādeḥ khalu prameyasya tattvajñānān niḥśreyasādhigamaḥ
children.translated_text: For the attainment of the highest good comes from true knowledge of the knowable object beginning with the self.

children.text: tac caitad uttarasūtreṇānūdyata iti ||
children.translated_text: And this same point is restated by the following sūtra.

children.text: heyam tasya nirvartakaṃ hānam ātyantikam tasyopāyo 'dhigantavya ity etāni catvāry arthapadāni samyag buddhvā niḥśreyasam adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: Having properly understood these four meaningful terms, namely what is to be abandoned, its producer, its complete abandonment, and the means to that which is to be attained, one attains the highest good.

children.text: tatra saṃśayādīnāṃ pṛthagvacanam anarthakam saṃśayādayo yathāsambhavaṃ pramāṇeṣu prameyeṣu cāntarbhavanto na vyatiricyanta iti satyam etat imās tu catasro vidyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ prāṇabhṛtām anugrahāyopadiśyante yāsāṃ caturthīyam ānvīkṣikī nyāyavidyā ||
children.translated_text: In this connection, it may be said that the separate mention of doubt and the rest is useless, since doubt and the rest, being included as appropriate among the pramāṇas and the knowable objects, are not distinct from them. This is true; nevertheless these four sciences are taught as having distinct starting points for the benefit of living beings, and the fourth among them is <s>ānvīkṣikī</s>, the science of Nyāya.

children.text: tasyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ saṃśayādayaḥ padārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that science, the categories such as doubt have distinct starting points.

children.text: teṣāṃ pṛthagvacanam antareṇādhyātmavidyāmātram iyaṃ syāt yathopaniṣadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without their separate mention, this would be merely a science of the self, like the Upaniṣads.

children.text: tasmāt saṃśayādibhiḥ padārthaiḥ pṛthak prasthāpyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is set forth separately by means of categories such as doubt.

children.text: tatra nānupalabdhe na nirṇīte 'rthe nyāyaḥ pravartate kiṃ tarhi saṃśayite 'rthe ||
children.translated_text: In that matter, Nyāya does not proceed with regard to an object that is not perceived, nor with regard to one that is already determined. With regard to what, then? With regard to an object that is in doubt.

children.text: yathoktaṃ vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyām arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: As has been stated: after deliberating, determination of the object by means of the thesis and counter-thesis is decision.

children.text: vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Deliberation is doubt.

children.text: pakṣapratipakṣau nyāyapravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The thesis and counter-thesis are the operation of Nyāya.

children.text: arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayas tattvajñānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Determination of the object is decision, that is, true knowledge.

children.text: sa ca ayaṃ kiṃsvid iti vastuvimarśamātram anavadhāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ prameye 'ntarbhavann evam arthaṃ pṛthag ucyate ||
children.translated_text: This, then, the mere deliberation about a thing as 'what might it be?', an indeterminate cognition, is doubt; although it is included among the knowable objects, it is stated separately for this purpose.

children.text: atha prayojanam yena prayuktaḥ pravartate tat prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: Next, purpose: that by which someone, being impelled, acts is the purpose.

children.text: yam artham abhīpsan jihāsan vā karmārabhate tenānena sarve prāṇinaḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi sarvāś ca vidyā vyāptāḥ tadāśrayaś ca nyāyaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever object a person desires to obtain or to abandon when he undertakes an action, by that object all living beings, all actions, and all sciences are pervaded; and Nyāya proceeds on that basis.

children.text: kaḥ punar ayaṃ nyāyaḥ pramāṇair arthaparīkṣaṇaṃ nyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What, then, is this Nyāya? Nyāya is the examination of objects by means of pramāṇas.

children.text: pratyakṣāgamāśritam anumānam sānvīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: Inference based on perception and authoritative testimony is investigation.

children.text: pratyakṣāgamābhyām īkṣitasyānvīkṣaṇam anvīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: Investigation is the further examination of what has been observed through perception and authoritative testimony.

children.text: tayā pravarttata ity ānvīkṣikī nyāyavidyā nyāyaśāstram ||
children.translated_text: Because it proceeds by that, it is called <s>ānvīkṣikī</s>, the science of Nyāya, the treatise on Nyāya.

children.text: yat punar anumānaṃ pratyakṣāgamaviruddhaṃ nyāyābhāsaḥ sa iti ||
children.translated_text: But inference that is opposed to perception and authoritative testimony is only an appearance of Nyāya.

children.text: tatra vādajalpau saprayojanau ||
children.translated_text: Among these, debate and wrangling have a purpose.

children.text: vitaṇḍā tu parīkṣyate ||
children.translated_text: But destructive criticism is examined.

children.text: vitaṇḍayā pravartamāno vaitaṇḍikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who proceeds by destructive criticism is a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s>.

children.text: sa prayojanam anuyukto yadi pratipadyate so 'sya pakṣaḥ so 'sya siddhānta iti vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti ||
children.translated_text: If, when questioned about his purpose, he accepts one, then that is his thesis and that is his established doctrine; thus he gives up the condition of being a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s>.

children.text: atha na pratipadyate nāyaṃ laukiko na parīkṣaka ity āpadyate ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not accept one, it follows that he is neither an ordinary person nor an examiner.

children.text: athāpi parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanaṃ bravīti etad api tādṛg eva ||
children.translated_text: And even if he says that his purpose is the making known of the refutation of the opponent's thesis, that too is just the same sort of thing.

children.text: yo jñāpayati yo jānāti yena jñāpyate yac ca jñāpyate etac ca pratipadyate yadi tadā vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti ||
children.translated_text: If he accepts the one who makes known, the one who knows, that by which it is made known, and what is made known, then he gives up the condition of being a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s>.

children.text: atha na pratipadyate parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanam ity etad asya vākyam anarthakaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not accept them, his statement, 'my purpose is the making known of the refutation of the opponent's thesis,' becomes meaningless.

children.text: vākyasamūhaś ca sthāpanāhīno vitaṇḍā tasya yady abhidheyaṃ pratipadyate so 'sya pakṣaḥ sthāpanīyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And destructive criticism is a collection of sentences without establishment. If he accepts something to be denoted by it, that becomes his thesis, something to be established.

children.text: atha na pratipadyate pralāpamātram anarthakaṃ bhavati vitaṇḍātvaṃ nivartata iti ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not accept it, it becomes mere prattle, meaningless, and the status of destructive criticism ceases.

children.text: atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣaviṣayo 'rthaḥ yatra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ darśanaṃ na vyāhanyate ||
children.translated_text: Next, an example is an object within the range of perception, where the observation of ordinary people and examiners is not contradicted.

children.text: sa ca prameyam ||
children.translated_text: And it is a knowable object.

children.text: tasya pṛthagvacanaṃ ca tadāśrayāv anumānāgamau tasmin sati syātām anumānāgamau asati ca na syātām ||
children.translated_text: Its separate mention is because inference and authoritative testimony rest upon it: when it exists, inference and authoritative testimony can exist; when it does not exist, they cannot exist.

children.text: tadāśrayā ca nyāyapravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The operation of Nyāya also rests upon it.

children.text: dṛṣṭāntavirodhena ca parapakṣapratiṣedho vacanīyo bhavati dṛṣṭāntasamādhinā ca svapakṣaḥ sādhanīyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By showing conflict with the example, one must state the refutation of the opponent's thesis; and by resolving the example, one's own thesis must be established.

children.text: nāstikaś ca dṛṣṭāntam abhyupagacchann āstikatvaṃ jahāti ||
children.translated_text: And a denier, in accepting an example, gives up being a denier.

children.text: anabhyupagacchan kiṃsādhanaḥ param upālabheteti ||
children.translated_text: If he does not accept it, by what means of proof could he reproach another?

children.text: niruktena ca dṛṣṭāntena śakyam abhidhātuṃ sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam tadviparyayād viparītam iti ||
children.translated_text: And with the example thus defined one can state: because of similarity to what is to be proved, the example in which that property exists is an illustration; from the opposite of that, there is the contrary one.

children.text: asty ayam ity anujñāyamāno 'rthaḥ siddhāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: An object that is admitted as 'this exists' is an established doctrine.

children.text: sa ca prameyam ||
children.translated_text: And it is a knowable object.

children.text: tasya pṛthagvacanaṃ satsu siddhāntabhedeṣu vādajalpavitaṇḍāḥ pravartante nāto 'nyatheti ||
children.translated_text: Its separate mention is because, when there are differences among established doctrines, debate, wrangling, and destructive criticism proceed, and not otherwise.

children.text: sādhanīyārthasya yāvati śabdasamūhe siddhiḥ parisamāpyate tasya pañcāvayavāḥ pratijñādayaḥ samūham apekṣyāvayavā ucyante ||
children.translated_text: The five members, beginning with the proposition, are called members with reference to the collection of words through which the establishment of the object to be proved is completed.

children.text: teṣu pramāṇasamavāyaḥ āgamaḥ pratijñā ||
children.translated_text: Among them there is the conjunction of pramāṇas: authoritative testimony is the proposition.

children.text: hetur anumānam ||
children.translated_text: The reason is inference.

children.text: udāharaṇaṃ pratyakṣam ||
children.translated_text: The example is perception.

children.text: upanayanam upamānam ||
children.translated_text: The application is comparison.

children.text: sarveṣām ekārthasamavāye sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanam iti ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is the showing of the force of all these when they inhere in one single object.

children.text: so 'yaṃ paramo nyāya iti ||
children.translated_text: This, then, is the highest form of <s>nyāya</s>.

children.text: etena vādajalpavitaṇḍāḥ pravartante nāto 'nyatheti ||
children.translated_text: By this means debate, wrangling, and cavil proceed, and not otherwise.

children.text: tadāśrayā ca tattvavyavasthā ||
children.translated_text: And the determination of reality depends upon it.

children.text: te caite 'vayavāḥ śabdaviśeṣāḥ santaḥ prameye 'ntarbhūtā evamarthaṃ pṛthag ucyanta iti
children.translated_text: Although these members, being particular forms of speech, are included within the knowable object, they are stated separately for this purpose.

children.text: tarko na pramāṇasaṃgṛhīto na pramāṇāntaram pramāṇānām anugrāhakas tattvajñānāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tarka</s> (reasoning) is not included among the means of knowledge, nor is it an additional means of knowledge; rather, as an aid to the means of knowledge, it serves for knowledge of reality.

children.text: tasyodāharaṇam kim idaṃ janma kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate āhosvid akṛtakena athākasmikam iti ||
children.translated_text: An example of it is this: is this birth produced by a made cause, or by an unmade cause, or is it accidental?

children.text: evam avijñāte 'rthe kāraṇopapattyā ūhaḥ pravarttate yadi kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate hetūcchedād upapanno 'yaṃ janmocchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the matter is not known in this way, supposition proceeds through the plausibility of causes: if it is produced by a made cause, then with the cutting off of the cause the cutting off of birth is reasonable.

children.text: athākṛtakena hetunā tato hetūcchedasyāśakyatvād anupapanno janmocchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if it is produced by an unmade cause, then, because the cutting off of the cause is impossible, the cutting off of birth is unreasonable.

children.text: athākasmikam ato 'kasmān nirvartyamānaṃ na punar nivartsyatīti nivṛttikāraṇaṃ nopapadyate tena janmānuccheda iti ||
children.translated_text: But if it is accidental, then, since what is produced accidentally will not again cease, no cause of cessation is reasonable; therefore there would be no cutting off of birth.

children.text: etasmiṃs tarkaviṣaye karmanimittaṃ janmeti pramāṇāni pravarttamānāni tarkeṇānugṛhante tattvajñānaviṣayasya vibhāgāt tattvajñānāya kalpate tarka iti ||
children.translated_text: In this field of reasoning, the means of knowledge that proceed toward the point that birth has karma as its cause are aided by reasoning; since the object of knowledge of reality has been differentiated, reasoning serves for knowledge of reality.

children.text: so 'yam itthambhūtas tarkaḥ pramāṇasahito vāde sādhanāyopālambhāya cārthasya bhavatīty evam arthaṃ pṛghag ucyate prameyāntarbhūto 'pīti ||
children.translated_text: Such reasoning of this sort, when accompanied by a means of knowledge, serves in debate both for establishing and for objecting to a point; for this purpose it is stated separately, even though it is included within the knowable object.

children.text: nirṇayas tattvajñānaṃ pramāṇānāṃ phalam tadavasāno vādaḥ tasya pālanārthaṃ jalpaviṭaṇḍe ||
children.translated_text: Ascertainment is knowledge of reality, the result of the means of knowledge. Debate ends in that; and wrangling and cavil exist for the protection of it.

children.text: tāv etau tarkanirṇayau lokayātrāṃ vahata iti ||
children.translated_text: These two, reasoning and ascertainment, sustain ordinary worldly procedure.

children.text: so 'yaṃ nirṇayaḥ prameyāntarbhūta evamarthaṃ pṛthag uddīṣṭa iti ||
children.translated_text: This ascertainment too is included within the knowable object, but for this purpose it is separately mentioned.

children.text: vādaḥ khalu nānāpravaktṛkaḥ pratyadhikaraṇasādhano 'nyatarādhikaraṇanirṇayāvasāno vākyasamūhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Debate, indeed, is a collection of statements made by different speakers, establishing opposing theses, and ending in the ascertainment of one or the other thesis.

children.text: pṛthag uddiṣṭa upalakṣaṇārtham ||
children.translated_text: It is separately mentioned for the purpose of indication.

children.text: upalakṣitena vyavahāras tattvajñānāya bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Through what is so indicated, practical procedure becomes conducive to knowledge of reality.

children.text: tadviśeṣau jalpavitaṇḍe tattvādhyavasāyasaṃrakṣaṇārtham ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: Its two special forms, wrangling and cavil, have been said to be for the protection of firm ascertainment of reality.

children.text: nigrahasthānebhyaḥ pṛthag uddhiṣṭā hetvābhāsā vāde codanīyā bhaviṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: Fallacious reasons are stated separately from points of defeat because they will have to be challenged in debate.

children.text: jalpavitaṇḍayos tu nigrahasthānānīti ||
children.translated_text: But in wrangling and cavil they are points of defeat.

children.text: chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ pṛthagupadeśa upalakṣaṇārtham iti ||
children.translated_text: The separate instruction concerning quibbles, futile rejoinders, and points of defeat is for the purpose of indication.

children.text: upalakṣitānāṃ svavākye parivarjanam chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ paravākye paryanuyogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When these quibbles, futile rejoinders, and points of defeat have been indicated, they are to be avoided in one's own speech, and in another's speech they are to be pressed by further questioning.

children.text: jāteś ca pareṇa prayujyamānāyāḥ sulabhaḥ samādhiḥ svayaṃ ca sukaraḥ prayoga iti ||
children.translated_text: And when a futile rejoinder is being used by the opponent, its answer is easy, and one's own use of it is easy as well.

children.text: seyam ānvīkṣikī pramāṇādibhiḥ padārthair vibhajyamānā
children.translated_text: This <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (science of inquiry), being divided according to the categories beginning with the means of knowledge,

children.text: pradīpaḥ sarvavidyānām upāyaḥ sarvakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: is proclaimed, in the enumeration of sciences, as the lamp of all sciences and the means for all actions,

children.text: āśrayaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ vidyoddeśe prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: and as the support of all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: tad idaṃ tattvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasādhigamārthaṃ yathāvidyaṃ veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this knowledge of reality is to be understood, according to the science, for the attainment of the highest good.

children.text: iha tv adhyātmavidyāyām ātmādijñānaṃ tattvajñānam ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, in the science of the self, knowledge of the self and the other listed objects is knowledge of reality.

children.text: niḥśreyasādhigamo 'pavargaprāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The attainment of the highest good is the attainment of liberation.

children.text: Chapter 2
āśugati manaḥ tasya bahiḥśarīrātmapradeśena jñānasaṃskṛtena sannikarṣaḥ pratyāgatasya ca prayatnotpādanam ubhayaṃ yujyata iti ||
children.translated_text: The mind is swift-moving. Its contact, outside the body, with a region of the self conditioned by cognition, and also its production of effort when it has returned, are both possible.

children.text: utpādya vā dhārakaṃ prayatnaṃ śarīrān niḥsaraṇaṃ manasaḥ atas tatropapannaṃ dhāraṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, after producing a sustaining effort, the mind's departure from the body follows; therefore concentration is reasonable there.

children.text: Chapter 3
icchādveṣaprayatnasukhaduḥkhajñānāny ātmano liṅgam ityataḥprabhṛti yathoktaṃ saṃgṛhyate tena bhūtendriyamanasāṃ caitanyapratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the statement that desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, and cognition are signs of the self, what has been stated is gathered together; by this the consciousness of the elements, senses, and mind is denied.

children.text: pāratantryāt paratantrāṇi bhūtendriyamanāṃsi dhāraṇapreraṇavyūhanakriyāsu prayatnavaśāt pravartante caitanye punaḥ svatantrāṇi syur iti ||
children.translated_text: Because of their dependence, the elements, senses, and mind are dependent; in acts of sustaining, impelling, and arranging they proceed under the control of effort. If they possessed consciousness, on the other hand, they would be independent.

children.text: akṛtābhyāgamācca pravṛttir vāgbuddhiśarīrārambha iti caitanye bhūtendriyamanasāṃ parakṛtaṃ karma puruṣeṇopabhujyata iti syād acaitanye tu tatsādhanasya svakṛtakarmaphalopabhogaḥ puruṣasyetyupapadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: And because otherwise there would be the arrival of what was not done by oneself: activity is the undertaking of speech, intellect, and body. If the elements, senses, and mind were conscious, then action done by another would be experienced by the person; but if they are unconscious, then it is reasonable that the person experiences the fruit of action done by himself through those instruments.

children.text: athāyaṃ siddhopasaṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now this is a summary of what has been established.

children.text: Chapter 4
upapadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: It is reasonable.

children.text: ātmana eva smaraṇaṃ na buddhisantatimātrasyeti ||
children.translated_text: Memory belongs to the self alone, not to a mere continuum of cognitions.

children.text: tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: The word 'tu' has the sense of restriction.

children.text: katham jñasvabhāvatvāt ||
children.translated_text: How so? Because its nature is that of a knower.

children.text: jña iti asya svabhāvaḥ svo dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Knower' means that this is its own nature, its own property.

children.text: ayaṃ khalu jñāsyati jānāti ajñāsīd iti trikālaviṣayeṇānekena jñānena sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: This self, indeed, is connected with many cognitions whose objects belong to the three times: 'it will know,' 'it knows,' and 'it knew.'

children.text: taccāsya trikālaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ pratyātmavedanīyaṃ jñāsyāmi jānāmi ajñāsiṣam iti vartate tad yasyāyaṃ svo dharmas tasya smaraṇaṃ na buddhiprabandhamātrasya nirātmakasyeti ||
children.translated_text: And this cognition of the three times belonging to it is directly experienced by each self as 'I shall know,' 'I know,' and 'I knew.' Therefore memory belongs to the one whose own property this is, not to a mere stream of cognition devoid of self.

children.text: smṛtihetūnām ayaugapadyād yugapad asmaraṇam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: It has been said that, because the causes of memory do not occur simultaneously, there is no simultaneous remembering.

children.text: atha kebhyaḥ smṛtir utpadyata iti smṛtiḥ khalu ||
children.translated_text: Now, from what does memory arise? Memory, indeed, arises from these:

children.text: Chapter 5
susmūrṣayā manaso dhāraṇaṃ praṇidhānaṃ susmūrṣitaliṅgacintanaṃ cārthasmṛtikāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: fixing the mind by the desire to remember, called attention, and reflection on a sign of what is desired to be remembered are causes of recollection of the object.

children.text: nibandhaḥ khalvekagranthopayamo 'rthānām ekagranthopayatāḥ khalvarthā anyonyasmṛtihetava ānupūrvyeṇetarathā vā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: A connection, indeed, is a bringing together of things into one treatise; for things brought together into one treatise become causes of mutual recollection, whether in sequence or otherwise.

children.text: dhāraṇaśāstrakṛto vā prajñāteṣu vastuṣu smartavyānām upanikṣepo nibandha iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, according to the authors of the science of retention, a connection is the depositing of things to be remembered among things already known.

children.text: abhyāsas tu samāne viṣaye jñānānām abhyāvṛttiḥ abhyāsajanitaḥ saṃskāra ātmaguṇo 'bhyāsaśabdenocyate sa ca smṛtihetuḥ samāna iti ||
children.translated_text: Practice, however, is the repeated occurrence of cognitions concerning the same object. The disposition produced by practice, a quality of the self, is denoted by the word practice, and it too is a cause of memory, because it is homogeneous with it.

children.text: liṅgaṃ punaḥ saṃyogi samavāyyekārthasamavāyi virodhi ceti ||
children.translated_text: A mark, again, is of four kinds: conjoined, inhering, inhering in one and the same substratum, and opposed.

children.text: yathā dhūmo 'gner gor viṣāṇaṃ pāṇiḥ pādasya rūpaṃ sparśasya abhūtaṃ bhūtasyeti ||
children.translated_text: For example, smoke is a mark of fire; a cow's horn of the cow; the hand of the foot; color of touch; and what is nonexistent of what is existent.

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ paśvavayavasthaṃ gotrasya smṛtihetur vidānām idaṃ gargāṇām idam iti ||
children.translated_text: A characteristic, located in an animal part, is a cause of remembering the clan: 'this belongs to the <s>Gargas</s>,' 'this belongs to them,' and so on.

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ citragataṃ pratirūpakaṃ devadattasyetyevamādi ||
children.translated_text: Resemblance is, for instance, a likeness in a picture, as of <s>Devadatta</s>, and the like.

children.text: parigrahāt svena vā svāmī svāminā vā svaṃ smaryate ||
children.translated_text: From possession, the owner is remembered by his property, or the property by its owner.

children.text: āśrayād grāmaṇyā tadadhīnaṃ saṃsmarati ||
children.translated_text: From a support, one remembers what is dependent on it, as a village headman remembers what is under his authority.

children.text: āśritāt tadadhīnena grāmaṇyam iti ||
children.translated_text: From what is supported, one remembers the village headman by means of what is under his authority.

children.text: sambandhād antevāsinā yuktaṃ guruṃ smarati ṛtvijā yājyam iti ||
children.translated_text: From relation, one remembers a teacher connected with his resident pupil, or the patron connected with his officiating priest.

children.text: ānantaryād iti karaṇīyeṣvartheṣu ||
children.translated_text: From immediacy, there is memory in regard to matters that are to be done next.

children.text: viyogād yena viyujyate tadviyogapratisaṃvedī bhṛśaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: From separation, one who experiences separation from that with which he is parted remembers it intensely.

children.text: ekakāryāt kartrantaradarśanāt kartrantare smṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From a single effect, on seeing one agent there is memory of another agent.

children.text: virodhād vijigīṣamāṇayor anyataradarśanād anyataraḥ smaryate ||
children.translated_text: From opposition, when one of two rivals seeking victory is seen, the other is remembered.

children.text: atiśayād yenātiśaya utpāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From excellence, one remembers the person by whom an excellence has been produced.

children.text: prāpteḥ yato 'nena kiṃcit prāptam āptavyaṃ vā bhavati tam abhīkṣṇaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: From acquisition, one repeatedly remembers the person from whom one has obtained something or from whom something is to be obtained.

children.text: vyavadhānāt kośādibhir asiprabhṛtīni smaryante ||
children.translated_text: From concealment, swords and the like are remembered by sheaths and similar things.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ taddhetuḥ smaryate ||
children.translated_text: Through pleasure and pain, their cause is remembered.

children.text: icchādveṣābhyāṃ yam icchati yaṃ ca dveṣṭi taṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: Through desire and hatred, one remembers the person whom one desires and the person whom one hates.

children.text: bhayād yato bibheti ||
children.translated_text: From fear, one remembers that from which one is afraid.

children.text: arthitvād yenārthī bhojanenācchādanena vā ||
children.translated_text: From need, one remembers that for which one is needy, whether food, clothing, or the like.

children.text: kriyayā rathena rathakāraṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: Through an action, one remembers a chariot-maker by a chariot.

children.text: rāgād yasyāṃ striyāṃ rakto bhavati tām abhīkṣṇaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: From passion, a man who is attached to a woman remembers her repeatedly.

children.text: dharmāj jātyantarasmaraṇam iha cādhītaśrutāvadhāraṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: From <s>dharma</s> (merit), there is recollection of another birth, and in this life the retaining of what has been learned and heard.

children.text: adharmāt prāganubhūtaduḥkhasādhanaṃ smarati ||
children.translated_text: From <s>adharma</s> (demerit), one remembers a previously experienced means of suffering.

children.text: na caiteṣu nimitteṣu yugapat saṃvedanāni bhavantīti yugapad asmaraṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: And since cognitions do not occur simultaneously in these causes, there is no simultaneous remembering.

children.text: nidarśanaṃ cedaṃ smṛtihetūnāṃ na parisaṃkhyānam iti ||
children.translated_text: This is an illustration of the causes of memory, not an exhaustive enumeration.

children.text: anityāyāṃ ca buddhāv utpannāpavargitvāt kālāntarāvasthānācca anityānāṃ saṃśayaḥ kim utpannāpavargiṇī buddhiḥ śabdavat āhosvit kālāntarāvasthāyinī kumbhavad iti ||
children.translated_text: And with respect to cognition as impermanent, because it ceases as soon as it has arisen and because impermanent things may also persist for some later time, there is a doubt: is cognition something that ceases as soon as it has arisen, like a sound, or does it remain for some later time, like a pot?

children.text: utpannāpavargiṇīti pakṣaḥ parigṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: The thesis accepted is that it ceases as soon as it has arisen.

children.text: kasmāt ||
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: Chapter 6
nāyam asti dṛṣṭāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no such example.

children.text: kasmāt akṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because it would entail the acceptance of what has not been established.

children.text: akṛtaṃ pramāṇato 'nupapannam tasyābhyāgamo 'bhyupapattir vyavasāya etacchraddadhānena pramāṇato 'nupapannaṃ mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: What is not established is what is not made out by a means of knowledge; its acceptance means admitting or determining it. By one who believes this, something not established by a means of knowledge would have to be regarded as true.

children.text: tasmān nāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto na pratyakṣaṃ na cānumānaṃ kiṃcid ucyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is not an example: no perception and no inference at all is being stated.

children.text: tad idaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya sādhyasamatvam abhidhīyata iti ||
children.translated_text: This is what is called the example's being equal to what is to be proved.

children.text: athavā nākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, it is not so, because of the consequence of accepting what is not established.

children.text: aṇuśyāmatādṛṣṭāntenākarmanimittāṃ śarīrotpattiṃ samādadhānasyākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who explains the production of the body as not caused by karma by means of the example of the dark color of atoms, there follows the consequence of accepting what is not established.

children.text: akṛte sukhaduḥkhahetau karmaṇi puruṣasya sukhaṃ duḥkham abhyāgacchatīti prasajyeta ||
children.translated_text: It would follow that pleasure and pain come to a person when the karma that is their cause of pleasure and pain has not been performed.

children.text: om iti bruvataḥ pratyakṣānumānāgamavirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who says 'yes' to this, there is contradiction with perception, inference, and authoritative tradition.

children.text: pratyakṣavirodhas tāvat bhinnam idaṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ pratyātmavedanīyatvāt pratyakṣaṃ sarvaśarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: First, there is contradiction with perception: this pleasure and pain is perceived by all embodied beings as distinct, because it is experienced by each self individually.

children.text: ko bhedaḥ tīvraṃ mandaṃ ciram āśu nānāprakāram ekaprakāram ityevamādir viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is the distinction? Differences such as intense and mild, long-lasting and quick, of many kinds and of one kind.

children.text: na cāsti pratyātmaniyataḥ sukhaduḥkhahetuviśeṣo na cāsati hetuviśeṣe phalaviśeṣo dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: And there is no particular cause of pleasure and pain fixed for each self; and when there is no particular difference of cause, no particular difference of effect is observed.

children.text: karmanimitte tu sukhaduḥkhayoge karmaṇāṃ tīvramandatopapatteḥ karmasañcayānāṃ cotkarṣāpakarṣabhāvāt nānāvidhaikavidhabhāvāc ca karmaṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhabhedopapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if the connection with pleasure and pain is caused by karma, the difference in pleasure and pain is intelligible, because karmas may be intense or mild, because accumulations of karma may increase or decrease, and because karmas may be of many kinds or of one kind.

children.text: so 'yaṃ hetubhedābhāvād dṛṣṭaḥ sukhaduḥkhabhedo na syād iti pratyakṣavirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the observed difference of pleasure and pain would not exist if there were no difference in causes; this is the contradiction with perception.

children.text: tathānumānavirodhaḥ dṛṣṭaṃ hi puruṣaguṇavyavasthānāt sukhaduḥkhavyavasthānam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise there is contradiction with inference, for the ordering of pleasure and pain is seen to depend on the ordering of qualities in a person.

children.text: yaḥ khalu cetanāvān sādhananirvartanīyaṃ sukhaṃ buddhvā tad īpsan sādhanāvāptaye prayatate sa sukhena yujyate na viparītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A conscious person who, having understood that pleasure is to be produced by certain means, desires it and strives to obtain those means, becomes joined with pleasure, not the opposite.

children.text: yaś ca sādhananirvartanīyaṃ duḥkhaṃ buddhvā tajjihāsuḥ sādhanaparivarjanāya yatate sa ca duḥkhena tyajyate na viparītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And one who, having understood that pain is to be produced by certain means, wishes to avoid it and strives to avoid those means, is freed from pain, not the opposite.

children.text: asti cedaṃ yatnam antareṇa cetanānāṃ sukhaduḥkhavyavasthānaṃ tenāpi cetanaguṇāntaravyavasthākṛtena bhavitavyam ity anumānam ||
children.translated_text: But there is also this ordering of pleasure and pain among conscious beings apart from effort; therefore it too must be caused by some other ordering of qualities in conscious beings. This is the inference.

children.text: tad etad akarmanimitte sukhaduḥkhayoge virudhyata iti ||
children.translated_text: That inference is contradicted if the connection with pleasure and pain is not caused by karma.

children.text: tacca guṇāntaram asaṃvedyatvād adṛṣṭaṃ vipākakālāniyamāc cāvyavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: And that, being another quality, is unseen because it is not directly apprehended, and it is indeterminate because there is no fixed rule for the time of its fruition.

children.text: buddhyādayas tu saṃvedyāś cāpavargiṇaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Cognitions and the like, however, are directly apprehended, and they belong to one who is destined for liberation.

children.text: athāgamavirodhaḥ bahu khalvidam ārṣam ṛṣīṇām upadeśajātam anuṣṭhānaparivarjanāśrayam upadeśaphalaṃ ca śarīriṇāṃ varṇāśramavibhāgeṇānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā pravṛttiḥ parivarjanalakṣaṇā nivṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, there is conflict with authoritative tradition. There is indeed much teaching of the seers, a body of instruction belonging to the sages, resting on performance and avoidance; and the fruit of instruction for embodied beings, according to the division of classes and life-stages, is activity characterized by performance and cessation characterized by avoidance.

children.text: taccobhayam etasyāṃ dṛṣṭau nāsti karma sucaritaṃ duścaritaṃ vā karmanimittaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhayogaḥ iti virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: But both of these are absent on this view: that there is no well-conducted or ill-conducted action, and no conjunction of pleasure and pain for persons caused by action. Thus it is contradicted.

children.text: seyaṃ pāpiṣṭhānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ akarmanimittā śarīrasṛṣṭir akarmanimittaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoga iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the very sinful false view: that the creation of the body has no action as its cause, and that the conjunction with pleasure and pain has no action as its cause.

children.text: Chapter 7
kena prakāreṇa kiṃdharmakāt kāraṇād vyaktaṃ śarīrādyutpadyata iti vyaktād bhūtasamākhyātāt pṛthivyāditaḥ paramasūkṣmān nityād vyaktaṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayopakaraṇādhāraṃ prajñātaṃ dravyam utpadyate ||
children.translated_text: In what way, and from a cause having what property, does the manifest body and so forth arise? From the manifest, known as the aggregate of elements, from earth and the rest, extremely subtle and eternal, there arises the manifest, known substance that is the body, senses, objects, instruments, and support.

children.text: vyaktaṃ ca khalvindriyagrāhyaṃ tatsāmānyāt kāraṇam api vyaktam ||
children.translated_text: And the manifest, indeed, is grasped by the senses; because of its common nature with that, the cause too is manifest.

children.text: kiṃ sāmānyaṃ rūpādiguṇayogaḥ rūpādiguṇayuktebhyaḥ pṛthivyādibhyo nityebhyo rūpādiguṇayuktaṃ śarīrādyutpadyate ||
children.translated_text: What is the common nature? Connection with qualities such as color. From eternal earth and the other elements, which are connected with qualities such as color, the body and so forth, connected with qualities such as color, arise.

children.text: pratyakṣaprāmāṇyād dṛṣṭo hi rūpādiguṇayuktebhyo mṛtprabhṛtibhyas tathābhūtasya dravyasyotpādaḥ tena cādṛṣṭasyānumānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Because of the validity of perception, the production of a substance of that same kind is observed from clay and similar things connected with qualities such as color; and through that there is inference of what is unseen.

children.text: rūpādīnām anvayadarśanāt prakṛtivikārayoḥ pṛthivyādīnāṃ nityānām atīndriyāṇāṃ kāraṇabhāvo 'numīyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Because the connection of color and the other qualities is observed in both original cause and modification, the causal status of earth and the other eternal, supersensible elements is inferred.
